description:
Surfaced via tmux-driven probes against the running interactive TUI
(wired to FakeTransport) plus direct OctoPi.Agent API tests. Compared
to upstream pi-mono in tmp/pi-mono/packages/{agent,coding-agent,tui}.

Investigation harness (still on disk, in .pi/tmp/queue-test):
  - probe_queue.exs       direct Agent API probes (FIFO, drain, abort, …)
  - tui_with_faux.exs     boots Interactive TUI with FakeTransport + a
                          /tmp/octo_pi_faux_release watch process so a
                          tmux driver can release scripted gates.
  - run_faux_tui.sh       launches the TUI for tmux capture.

Observed behavior summary (vs upstream):

1. Steering queue is never drained at run start or after non-tool turns.
   Items steered before/during a single-turn run sit in the queue forever.
2. Submit-while-streaming in the TUI calls Coder.prompt (not steer/follow_up)
   so queued messages are dropped at the agent (returns {:error, :already_streaming}
   which the TUI swallows) and only appear in the local transcript.
3. There is no in-input "Steering: …" / "Follow-up: …" pending-messages
   indicator. Users get no visual confirmation a message is queued.
4. Public Agent.drain_steering / drain_follow_up honor the queue's drainage
   mode (default :one_at_a_time → returns 1 of N). The dequeue overlay
   therefore only ever shows one item.
5. Dequeue overlay UX diverges from upstream: upstream restores all queued
   messages back into the editor for free editing; octo_pi shows an overlay
   with arrow-key + Backspace per-item delete. No way to edit the *text* of
   a queued item.
6. Dequeue overlay's Escape "re-enqueue" path uses to_string(msg.content)
   which crashes for list-content messages.
7. Coder.steer / Coder.follow_up swallow {:error, :full} from the agent
   and always return :ok. Caller cannot detect bound rejection.
8. Abort during a run does not clear queues — matches upstream — but the
   TUI's escape handler does not implement the upstream
   restoreQueuedMessagesToEditor({abort: true}) flow.

Sub-tickets break these out individually.
title: [EPIC] Prompt-queue parity & UX gaps vs pi-mono
